substantive_delta: The frozen proof partitions each chronological cross-step by the moved label and the first coordinate attaining the target minimum, keeping the whole other-label tuple as one context. This gives at most O_k((N/b)^(k-1)) exact b-by-b times b-by-b^(k-1) Boolean products per dyadic node, with repeated packing and scattering charged. The resulting global sum yields deterministic O_k(m+n+n^(k+0.3)) detection for every fixed k>=3 under the unchanged source weight-operation model. The k=3, delta=0.7 consequence resolves the entire immutable existential original.
why_nonroutine: The prior tuple graph has O(m n^(k-1)) explicit transitions. Applying generic transitive closure to N^k tuple states, merely mentioning fast multiplication, or contracting unrestricted outputs at every node does not provide the new bound. The exact output classes are needed both to preserve dependency order and to reduce the product count while allowing the moved coordinate beyond the current interval. The proof establishes that structural scheduling step and its complete dyadic data-movement analysis. Shortest-path filtering, tuple semantics, completion devices, generic recursion, multiplication exponents and the rational conversion principles remain credited prior tools. No equivalent full theorem was found in the bounded current primary-source search; this is not an exhaustive priority certificate.
significance: This breaks the dense n^(k+1) exponent for the unrestricted positive-weight prescribed shortest-path problem, rather than a sparse, bounded-width, unweighted or other restricted subclass. It answers AVW Open Problem 3 and gives the same constant saving for every fixed k>=3. The proved common-order labelled-graph theorem also covers ordinary prescribed disjoint paths. These consequences constitute substantive mathematical value. Whether the compact new scheduling argument and currently demonstrated consequences meet the higher STOC depth and breadth threshold remains separately uncertain, so mathematical acceptance does not promote the venue label.
